newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - FEB 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - FEB 3.

text.p: THIS PRESS DIGEST CONTAINS ESTONIA, CZECH REPUBLIC, LITHUANIA, SLOVAKIA, LATVIA AND CROATIA.
ESTONIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The United Popular Party of Estonia of mainly Russian-speakers, held its congress on Saturday and approved a programme aimed at integrating Russian-speakers into Estonian society. Viktor Andreyev was re-elected as chairman of the party. The party is also attempting to restore the Russian parliament faction, which broke up last December.
SONUMILEHT
- Coalition Party is amazed at the recommendation by Centre Party leader Edgar Savisaar that Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi should resign.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Investigators are looking into allegations linking the transfer of 10 million to a Swiss bank in 1993 and the murder of a bank official last January.
- Opposition Reform Party leader Siim Kallas declared that no political cooperation negotiations were held during the Turkish visit of an Estonian delegation, attended by Kallas and Savisaar.
POSTIMEES
- Radical nationalist and patriotic organisations met in Tartu on Sunday and held a meeting to mark the anniversary of the 1920 Tartu Peace Treaty.
ARIPAEV
- The firm, which organises car parking in central Tallinn, has fined citizens illegally and has to repay some of the fines.
- The Wermo furniture firm is selling its products in Japan and has recently made contacts with traders in Singapore and South Korea.
-- Riga Newsroom, +371 721 5240 CZECH REPUBLIC

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Last year, construction savings once again beat the previous record. The total amount of money stored in construction savings banks increased over 1995 by about 20 billion to reach 34.5 billion crowns.

- Directors of Trustfin, a subsidiary of Zbrojovka Vsetin, have decided to issue shares amounting to 240 to 500 million crowns destined mainly for the American capital market. The shares should be issued this autumn and will have a nominal value of 100 crowns each.
- Prague Agrobanka, which is currently under compulsory administration, took over Plzenska Banka (PB) from Motoinvest last Friday. Agrobanka plans to turn PB into an investment or mortgage bank.

- So far no one has entered the public tender for the sale of 100 percent of shares in Eska Cheb, a significant manufacturer of bicycles, which made nearly 40,000 bicycles last year solely for export.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Without much warning, railway workers have decided to begin a strike tomorrow for a minimum of two days, which will stop operation of all railways, disrupting life for thousands of people and many businesses.

- Large hospitals which have debts of hundreds of millions of crowns do not always manage to settle their accounts with health insurance companies. If hospital directors do not resolve their financial problems soon, health insurance companies are also in store for a crisis.

PRAVO - President Havel stated in an interview on Czech radio yesterday that Chairman of Parliament Milos Zeman's suspicions and accusations of illegal activities of the secret service (BIS) are not a sufficient reason to remove Zeman from his position.

- Beginning April 1, the price of stamps for letters going to foreign countries will increase on average by 5.8 percent, while the price of parcels will decrease by approximately 1.7 percent. --Prague Newsroom 42-2-24-23-0003
LITHUANIA
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- An explosion blew up a car and killed Juras Abromavicius, 38, in Kaunas on Friday night. Abromavicius was the head of the Kaunas headquarters of the volunteer defence force.
- Political prisoners are negative over parliament's plans to pass KGB, Soviet interior ministry and Communist Party archives to a research centre on genocide and resistance.

- Investment bank Williams de Broe will seek to become one of the most active international financial institutions in Lithuania's financial markets. It said it will take part in privatisation and invest in equity market.
- Russian Gazprom will not cut gas supplies to Lithuania after the country transferred 15 million on Friday. Lithuanian Gas still owes 13 million to Stella Vitae.
RESPUBLIKA

- Poland's ambassador to Lithuania sent secret telegrams about the situation in Latvia and its position on joining NATO and the European Union from Vilnius uncoded. The information was of major interest to Russia's secret services.
- Hermis Bank suspended trade in its shares on before an annual shareholders' meeting on February 12. It is expected that the meeting will support boosting the share capital of the bank.

- A World Bank mission arrived on Sunday for two weeks to discuss an 80 million structural adjustment loan. The first 40 million of the credit was received last October and the second tranche is expected in March. -- Riga Newsroom, +371 721 5240
SLOVAKIA
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said last year's foreign trade deficit of 64.3 billion crowns was not a reason to devalue the crown.
- Kozlik said the stable economic development would require a closer look at developments in wages, which should reflect economic productivity.
NARODNA OBRODA - The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) said the postponement of banking privatisation beyond March 31 would not endanger Slovakia's attempts to join the OECD.
- The private TV channel Markiza said it was considering taking part in a privatisation tender for one of the two terrestrial networks currently operated by the official Slovak Television STV.

- The Bratislava plant of German car producer VW completed 30,147 cars in 1996, some 371 units more than originally planned. According to preliminary calculations, the value of overall production totalled some 18 billion crowns.
- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said it would draft a law that would allow citizens access to files of former communist secrete police.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said the proposed indefinite postponement of bank privatisation would have a negative impact on the entire economy and could delay Slovakia's entry to OECD.
- The Slovak banking sector fulfilled this year's second minimum reserves requirements at 1.34 percent above the required amount.
PRAVDA - Damage after the fire that last weekend broke out in the hygienic paper producer PT Zilina is estimated at some 100 million crowns. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
LATVIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Fatherland & Freedom, the third largest government party, wants to keep the posts of economy and justice ministers in the new government.
- A group of 27 Latvian peacekeepers left for Denmark on Sunday for training to later participate in peace-keeping operations in Bosnia.
- A demonstration of several hundred gathered at the 1905 revolution monument in Riga on Saturday to protest against the increase of rent and public utility tariffs.
- The state budget in January shows almost six million lats of surplus. Ministry of Finance is meanwhile looking for resources to fill a gap in local government budgets.
- Latvia's Industrialists Confederation believes that state electricity firm Latvenergo has no economic reasons to raise electricity tariffs.
DIENA
- The draft law on refugees and asylum-seekers is ready to be handed in to the cabinet. The law is seen as key to allowing visa-free travel to Scandinavia.
BIZNES & BALTIYA

- Norwegian Varner Baltija bought a supermarket in the Europe Centre, in Riga, which was intended as the biggest in the Baltic states. The building is believed to be connected to a string of murders last year.

- It is likely that the French state-owned gas concern Gaz de France will become the second strategic investor in Latvian Gas, instead of the German consortium formed by Preussen Elektra and Ruhrgas. The Germans withdrew their bid after analysing the financial situation of the company.
- A draft law on money laundering will be submitted to the cabinet.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The legal director of the Latvian Privatisation Agency says the land market in Latvia is still under too many restrictions. -- Riga Newsroom +371 721 5240
CROATIA
VJESNIK
- Croatian top player Goran Ivanisevic wins Croatian's Indoors Tournament in a dramatic finale after beating British Greg Rusedski.

- Road link between Zagreb and the main port of Rijeka to be shortened with a new stretch of highway that should be completed before the summer. The country plans to build some 1,600 kilometers of new roads before the year 2005 and invest 49.3 billion.
- United Nations soldiers payed last respects to the Belgian corporal killed in a shooting incident in Eastern Slavonia.
- Tennants of state-owned apartments will be able to transfer their right to household members according to new law.
VECERNJI LIST
- Railway between Osijek and Beli Manastir on the Hungarian border, crossing last Serb pocket in Croatia, should open in February.
- Prices of veterinarian services to be reduced, depending on a number of animals on a certain farm, according new state regulations.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Ailiing Croatian Railways should lay off 7,000 workers and close 400 kilometres of railroads to recover from current losses, Ministry of transport says in a report.
- Is sunshine too expensive? Hotel Amfora on Hvar island starts a pilot-programme for consistent use of solar energy. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
